title: Good King Wenceslas
description: Good King Wenceslas in Tonic Solfa (doh is G): the solfa with the words, staff notation, all five verses and a piano, for carol services.
about: John Mason Neale wrote these words in 1853 to a spring carol melody, TEMPUS ADEST FLORIDUM, from the Finnish-Swedish song book Piae Cantiones (1582). The story is about Wenceslas, a tenth-century Duke of Bohemia, and his page going out in the snow to help a poor man on the feast of Stephen, the day after Christmas.
The verses are written as a conversation, so many choirs give the king's lines to the men and the page's lines to the women.
underlay: Good King Wen-ces-las looked out On the feast of Ste-phen, When the snow lay round a-bout, Deep and crisp and e-ven; Bright-ly shone the moon that night, Though the frost was cru-el, When a poor man came in sight, Gath-’ring win-ter fu_-el.

lines: When the snow lay round about,
Brightly shone the moon that night,
When a poor man came in sight,
“Sire, he lives a good league hence,
“Bring me flesh, and bring me wine,
Thou and I will see him dine,
Page and monarch, forth they went,
Through the rude wind’s wild lament
Fails my heart, I know not how;
Thou shalt find the winter’s rage
In his master’s steps he trod,
Heat was in the very sod
Ye who now will bless the poor
